rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE PRACTICE OF REAL ESTATE SERVICE IN THE PHILIPPINES, CREATING A REAL ESTATE COMMISSION AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to do away with the duplication of jurisdictional responsibility in the direction and management of activities of real estate brokers and allied professionals who must strictly adhere to a National Code of Ethics the Commission willadopt; and most importantly, will ferret out the unauthorized practitioners who control practically 75% of the real estate transactions in the Philippines which consequently had jeopardized the stability of this industry as it had victimized real estate buyers.

rows.author: C073
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING ALL AGENCIES IN THE EXECUTIVE DEPARTMENT TO SUBMIT A POVERTY ALLEVIATION IMPACT STATEMENT (PAIS) IN THE PROPOSED BUDGET OF EACH DEPARTMENT FOR CONSIDERATION IN THE ANNUAL GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS ACT
rows.abstract: Rationale: Amelioration of the lot of the poor should be a principal yardstick of all government activity, from planning all the way to execution. This should be part of the bureaucratic consciousness. Pro-poor considerations should be integrated into all planning and execution by government. > The Poverty Alleviation Impact Statement (PAIS) should address the two core issues that are associated with poverty problem - income generation and income enhancement. Such a statement should accompany all budgeted program and project proposals presented to Congress so that as early as budget preparation, poverty alleviation considerations are imbued in the bureaucratic mindset.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2001-08-20

rows.author: D073
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING ADDITIONAL TAX DEDUCTIONS FOR INDIVIDUAL INCOME EARNERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION THIRTY- FOUR OF `THE TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997'
rows.abstract: THE AMOUNT OF TUITION OR MATRICULATION FEES PAID FOR BY THE TAXPAYER IN FAVOR OF HIS CHILDREN ATTENDING SCHOOL SHALL BE ALLOWED AS A DEDUCTION FROM HIS GROSS INCOME: PROVIDED, THAT THE FAMILY OF THE SAID TAXPAYER HAS A GROSS INCOME OF NOT MORE THANTWO HUNDRED FIFTY THOUSAND PESOS (P250,000.00) FOR THE TAXABLE YEAR: PROVIDED, FURTHER, THAT THE SAID DEDUCTION SHALL APPLY ONLY TO THREE (3) DEPENDENTS OF THE TAXPAYER: PROVIDED, FINALLY, THAT IN THE CASE OF MARRIED TAXPAYERS, ONLY THE SPOUSE CLAIMING THE ADDITIONAL EXEMPTION FOR DEPENDENTS SHALL BE ENTITLED TO THIS DEDUCTION. > ANY AMOUNT PAID BY AN INDIVIDUAL TAXPAYER AS INTEREST ON HOME LOAN MORTGAGES SHALL BE ALLOWED AS DEDUCTION FROM HIS GROSS INCOME.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-08-20

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO LIBERALIZE PHILIPPINE CIVIL AVIATION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Since 98% of visitors to the Philippines arrive and express cargo services can only be maintained by air transport, civil aviation has become a vital infrastructure for establishing access to the Philippines. By providing "highways in theskies", it links our country to world thereby facilitating our participation in the mainstreams of tourist traffic movement, and the flow of trade and investments. Without such links, we are faced with the dire prospects of economic stagnation arising from isolation.> To ACCELERATE the process of LIBERALIZATION, this bill seeks to: (1) alter the Civil Aeronautics Board (CAB) Composition, and streamline its procedures; (2) declare a civil aviation policy; and (3) impose policy guidelines and dirrections for CAB to observe and implement.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2001-08-20

rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING ANY GOVERNMENT OFFICIAL WHO REFUSES TO RELEASE IMMEDIATELY A DETAINED PRISONER WHO HAS POSTED BAIL AND/OR CLEARED OF CHARGES BY COMPETENT AUTHORITIES
rows.abstract: Any government official in any branch of the government who refuses to release immediately a detained prisoner after psoting bail or cleared of the charges by competent authorities shall be punished with an imprisonment equivalent to the penalty provided for by law for the crime for which the illegally detained person has been charged and a fine of not less than Thirty Thousand Pesos (P30,000.00). The law on conspiracy shall aplly in this case.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-08-20

rows.abstract: This law applies to all government employees in civil service, all branches, subdivisions, instrumentaliti es, and agencies of the Government including government-owne d and controlled corporations with original charters.> All government employees'organization shall have the right to engage in peaceful concerted activities for the purpose of collective negotiation or for their mutual benefit and for furtherance and protection of their interest. rows.abstract: This proposed measure seeks to create a "special agricultural fund" to be taken-out of the ten percent annual gross income of the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR) for the years 2001 to 2010 to be administered by the Landbank of the Philippines for lending to small farmers and fisherfolks individually or thru their cooperatives. > This proposed measure further addresses the call of President Glorian Macapagal-Arroy o for the enactment of a law making farm lands acceptable asloal collateral to increase investments in agriculture. In addition to farmlands, the bill provides that small farmers and fisherfolks can use their farming and fishing implements, crops and expected fish harvests as collateral to avail of this crediit facility.

Rationale: At present, it is the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) and Land Transportation Office (LTO) that regulate and issue franchises in the operation of filcabs. > Considering that it is the Sangguniang of Cities and Municipalities under the Local Government Code that regulate and issue franchises regarding tricycles, it would be more appropriate for the same sangguniang to regulate and issue franchises with regard to the filcabs.> This bill is therefore, proposed so that filcabs are regulated through the local government units, which are in a better position to determine its use and desirability in their respective areass of jurisdiction.

rows.abstract: This bill considers as ACTS OF DISCRIMINATION the following: (1) Giving UNDUE FAVOR OR PREFERENCE to a male applicant over a female applicant in the RECRUITMENT of employees; (2) GIVING UNDUE FAVOR TO A MALE EMPLOYEE OVER A FEMALE EMPLOYEE WITH RESPECT TO DISMISSAL OR RETRENCHMENT; and (3) AND ALL OTHER ANALOGOUS DISCRIMINATORY ACTS. FOR THE PURPOSE OF THE PRECEDING ARTICLE THE TERM "GIVING UNDUE FAVOR" MEANS TREATING DIFFERENTLY A WOMAN FROM AN ACTUAL OR HYPOTHETICAL MALE UNDER SUBSTANTIALLY SIMILAR JOB DESCRIPTIONS QUALIFICATIONS AND CIRCUMSTANCES; OR SUCH FAVOR WAS GRANTED OR EXERCISED IN VIOLATION OF REASONABLE JOB DESCRIPTION OR EQUAL OPPORTUNITY SYSTEM AS PROVIDED IN THE SUCCEEDING OR A CONDITION OR REQUIREMENT HAS BEEN APPLIED TO HEER AND THAT CONSIDERABLY FEWER WOMEN THAN MEN ARE ABLE TO COMPLY WITH THE CONDITION WHEN SUCH CONDITION IS NEGLIGIBLE TO THE PERFORMANCE OF THE JOB. Sec. 2. (4) TO DENY ANY WOMAN THE BENEFITS OF EMPLOYMENT OR OTHER STATUTORY BENEFITS UNDER OUR LAWS B

rows.abstract: "Family Living Wage Act of 2001."  For purposes of this Act, employees and workers who are considered to be regular wage earners shall be entitled to enjoy the family living wage.  The State shall institutionaliz e a mechanism to implement a fairer,more acceptable and constitutionall y guaranteed wage system based on the current family living standard of employees and workers in the public and private sectors. Employees and workers in public and private sectors shall be entitled to receive a family living wage equivalent to the daily cost of living of an  average Filipino family which average size shall be determine by the National Statistics Office (NSO) and the Commission on Population (POPCOM) as it may be deemed necessary.

rows.abstract: The Secretary of the Department of Finance is hereby mandated to prescribe, on or before January 31 of each taxable year, a minimum occupancy rate and a daily room rate for motels and inns which will serve as basis for the computation of gross receipts of proprietors, operators and keepers of such establishments. The minimum occupancy and daily room rates shall be prescribed on a regional basis: Provided, That the minimum occupancy rate shall in no case be lower than eighty percent (80%) of motel or inn capacity for establishments situated within Metro Manila, and sixty percent (60%) for establishments situated in other highly urbanized cities and chartered cities: Provided, further, That the imposition of the minimum rates as herein mandaated may be suspended due to force majeure, prolonged labor dispute or other legitimate business reverses.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING PUBLIC OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES TO SUBMIT A WRITTEN PERMISSION OR WAIVER IN FAVOR OF THE OMBUDSMAN TO LOOK INTO ALL DEPOSITS OF WHATEVER NATURE WITH BANKS OR BANKING INSTITUTIONS BOTH WITHIN AND OUTSIDE THE PHILIPPINES INCLUDING INVESTMENT BONDS ISSUED BY THE GOVERNMENT OF THE PHILIPPINES, ITS POLITICAL SUBDIVISIONS AND INSTRUMENTALITI ES, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Previous laws, such as those requiring the submission of statements of assets and liabilities, providing forfeiture in favor of the state of property unlawfully acquired, a code of conduct and ethical standards, and even that providing for the creation of the Office of the Ombudsman have proven insufficient and somewhat still lacking if we are to base its success on the absence or lack of acts of corruption in government. It is for this reason that this bill was filed.  To add to those laws which, in one way or the other, seek to tighten the noose on grafters by requiring an even greater amount of transparency among public officials and employees.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Turncoatism, most often, is the result of political patronage, or hope of greater patronage from the party in power.  Party platforms and ideologies are eschewed in exchange for patronage. This practice certainly is preventing and not helping in the development of a strong multi-party system.  In order to minimize politics of patronage and develop a strong multi-party system in the Philippines, it is the purpose of this bill to prohibit political turncoatism and provide penalties therefore.

rows.abstract: The Philippine Oil Corporation, Domicile and Term. - There is hereby created a body corporate to be known as the Philippine Oil Corporation, hereinafter referred to as the "Corporation" which shall monitor and control the country's requirements forrefined petroleum products and shall integrate the refining, marketing and distribution functions to meet the domestic oil requirement. The principal office of the Corporation shall be determined by its Board of Directors.  It may establish such officers, agencies, subsidiaries, branches or correspondents in the Philippines or abroad as its business operations would require. The Corporation shall have a term of fifty (50) years from the creation hereof, which shall be deemed renewed for an equall period unless sooner dissolved by law.
